newsitem.title: EGYPT: Militants kill four civilian guards in south Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Militants kill four civilian guards in south Egypt.

text.p: Suspected Moslem militants have gunned down four civilian guards who were helping police protect a southern Egyptian village, the interior ministry and security sources said on Saturday.

The ministry said the gunmen -- believed to be members of the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) fighting to overthrow the government -- shot the men on Friday outside a mosque in Tel Zayed village after evening prayers.
It named the men as Aly Younes, Farag al-Haq, Khairy Atta and Essam Mohammed. Tel Zayed is located some 345 km (215 miles) south of Cairo.
Security sources say police in the south have recently recruited and armed civilians to help protect villages in the south which has become a hotbed of Moslem militancy.
On Friday, suspected Gama'a members killed at least five people in three separate attacks on southern villages.
More than 970 people have been killed and scores wounded since Moslem militant groups began an armed struggle four years ago to topple the government and establish an Islamic state in Egypt.
